totality-types-callsites.verdict:
NOT CERTIFIABLE. I read all 6217 lines and verified every repository claim by loading the modules in process (ActionCapabilityRegistry.list() = 226, canonicalProductionPolicyDefinitions() = 221, MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG = 47, C9_CAPABILITIES = 56 — all at baseline). Against the owner bar of 0/0/0 I find 7 structural violations, 1 security-contract violation and 3 unproven normative claims.

What the consolidation got right, said plainly: the two disclosed floor reductions are exactly two, both in §0.17, and no other clause creates a third — the `RISK_FLOOR['read']`, `C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR['SOURCE_READ']`, `EFFECT_FLOOR['CONTROL']` and `targetFloor('c')` values are each argued as removing a spurious raise or a double-count, not as reductions. §2.6.7's CLIENT.2 (`pii_ceiling: 'client_identified'`) and §2.6.22's ARTIFACT.3 (`contains_pii`) are intact and correctly unrenumbered, with CLIENT.3 and ARTIFACT.5 sitting beside them as the role clauses, not over them. Gate 5 is recomputable: §3.7's IntentRecord carries all six of F43's inputs. Gate 6 dispatches on `subjectCapability(record)` bound once, and is scoped by effect so a HANDOFF resolves destination fences only. Every repaired semantic on the checklist survived the fold — AuthorityHint's closed non-authority members, the CapabilityRef-typed `handoff_capability_ref`, FloorSubject, `c9Floor` calling only non-throwing accessors, `nameSourceOf` binding `el` in all seven branches, InteractiveRef's seven members, the filtered-then-appended reading order with escape last, the ref-kind:role suffix descriptor with base and pointer list, both catalogues keyed `id@version`, and `render_tier` inside `body_hash`.

What fails. The consolidation folded most errata but left three uncorrected, and each is a live rule today. (1) §2.6.5 BOOK.2 still states the `requiredConfirmationKind` chain with a `SETTINGS_DRAFT` default branch that §0.13 F72 deletes as \"not a fence\" — I executed that chain against the live registry and reproduced F72's own figure exactly: 94 of the 105 widget-reachable capabilities route onto a COMMIT-bearing kind, consent recording among them. Three further normative clauses (SETTINGS.1, FORM.2, and Annex A's NORMATIVE A1.6.2) name BOOK.2's derivation as their governing mechanism, so the fail-open form is load-bearing in four places. Annex B EB-8 shows it was voided once already. (2) §3.10.1 still allowlists the four appointment-detail capabilities that F34/F37 gap-key, which makes F31's start-up assertion set unpassable; Annex B EC-1 shows that correction too was written and not folded. (3) §3.7 still classifies `frozen_nouns` as conversation content inside a code-block divider, contradicting F14 and §4.4.3 — and that is what breaks FR-12, whose one enforcing mechanism is F15's reachability test. Nineteen of the twenty-one FR rows hold (most fail-closed because the widget layer does not exist in any form, which the contract states honestly and I confirm); FR-12 does not hold as a checked property, and FR-6a/FR-6b hold only because §0 outranks the clauses that would defeat them.

Beyond those: `draft_class` and `Phrase` are each declared twice with drifted members; the five floor tables are declared twice byte-identically under a sentence asserting they are declared once; and Annex A — normative, and given precedence over §§1–4 — is written entirely against the retired Section-0 numbering, with 31 citations to seventeen subsections that do not exist and five erratum citations (E-16, E-18, E-19, E-20, E-30) in normative text. The preamble's claim that the contract has \"no errata layer and no precedence chain\" is contradicted by A0.2, which declares one; and every finding above is a case where a reader must follow a correction to learn what a rule says, which is exactly what the preamble promises they never need to do. The fixes are mechanical and none requires a semantic change: fold the three missed errata, delete four duplicate declarations, and run one renumbering pass over every Section-0 cross-reference.

NOT CERTIFIABLE. The owner bar is 0/0/0; the count is 12 structural violations, 0 security-contract violations, 2 unproven normative claims.

What passed, and it is a great deal. Every cardinality claim in §0 verifies exactly against the executed registries — 226/221/47/56, the nine C9 extras by name, AE ∩ (C9 ∪ TOOL) = ∅, MONEY 92/39 against 12/4 for the bare token, BOOKING 13/7, CONSENT 3, IDENTITY 6, MARKETING_FANOUT 4, TENANT_AUTHORITY 28/14, policyDecision 129/95/2, 53 unreachable and 105 reachable, 98 facet tokens, the seven autonomyLevel counts, mode 41/13/2, resourceClass 40/15/1 with the single LOCAL row being c9.no_action, riskTier with zero 'restricted', RUN_OPENING 15. Not one number is off. Every item on the explicit survival list is intact: exactly two floor reductions, both in §0.17, and no third clause creates one; §2.6.7 CLIENT.2 and §2.6.22 ARTIFACT.3 are present, unrenumbered, and not superseded by CLIENT.3 / ARTIFACT.5; Gate 5 recomputes verificationFloor from an IntentRecord (FloorSubject is structural and IntentRecord carries effect, capability, handoff_capability_ref, target, priority and widget_kind); Gate 6 dispatches on subjectCapability and is scoped by effect so a HANDOFF resolves destination fences only; AuthorityHint's member set is closed and non-authority; FLOOR_EXEMPT and verificationFloor are over FloorSubject; c9Floor calls only tryGet and ReadonlyMap.get; nameSourceOf binds `el` in all seven branches; InteractiveRef has seven members; reading_order filters produced against emitted then appends the closed form with escape last; accessible_name_suffix keys `${ref.k}:${role}` with base plus pointer list; NARRATIVE_TEMPLATES and MOMENT_TEMPLATES are keyed id@version; render_tier is a body_hash term. All twenty-one FR rows hold, and the status column is honest — fourteen hold only fail-closed because a component is absent, and the document says so rather than hiding it.

Why it still fails. The consolidation folded the errata into §0 and Annex A but did not finish the sweep through §§1–4. Six of the twelve structural violations are stale text that an erratum already corrected once and the fold left behind in a second, still-normative place: §3.10.1 still calls the four appointment-detail capabilities "allowlisted" after EC-1 gap-ledgered them and F34/F37 record the correction; §2.4 and §2.6.13 still name the deleted `orchestration.run.read` as a registry key; §2.6.16's draft_class still carries the two members EB-9 voided; §2.3.1 still re-declares Phrase without `params`; §4.4.2 is still the 17-row table EB-13/EB-15 raised to 22 everywhere else; F66 still names three `intent_token` members that no shape declares. Three of these make a start-up assertion set unpassable rather than merely mis-documenting: the allowlist/gap XOR, §2.1's per-kind totality over the retention table, and RT5's column-classification totality (`approval_of_intent_ref` is classified nowhere).

The deepest finding is the precedence contradiction. The preamble's first rule is that there is no precedence chain; A0.2 declares "Section 0 > Annex A > §§1–4". That chain is not decorative — it is the only thing that resolves §3.10.1 against F34, A1.6.2 against F28, and §2.4 row 16 against F79. The document cannot both deny having a precedence chain and depend on one to be readable.

Nothing here is a security-contract violation, and I want to say that plainly rather than reach for one. The §3.10.1 allowlist contradiction is the closest: the four capabilities carry twelve actor roles including CLIENT, approvalRequirement NONE, and three of them no clientPrincipalTarget, so a button on them would confer authority the widget does not hold. But it is caught fail-closed — with no propose key there is no AE_PROPOSE_PAIRING row, F31's pairing assertion and its (row XOR gap) clause both fail, and the process does not start. Under the prompt's own carve-out that is not a security-contract violation, and I have recorded it as structural with the exposure stated so it can be adjudicated. Every other conferral path I traced terminates in a gap key, a veto, or an unreachable STEP_UP_VERIFIED.

The two unproven claims are both in clauses whose enforcing mechanism was deleted or was never declared: A1.6.2 mandates a WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY row over an AE-CAP key, which F28 forbids, and names an EP-REGISTRY-LOAD assertion (personal_data disjointness) that F31 does not contain; CLIENT.2's sole named mechanism is the "display fence" that §0.19 item 3 declares does not exist, and the stated remainder cannot refuse an emission. Both are one-clause repairs.

Every finding is a bounded edit — a word in a table row, five missing rows, a deleted duplicate, one mechanism sentence. None requires a design change. The substance of this contract — the key-space discipline, the positive allowlist over an open facet vocabulary, the derived floor with its fail-closed defaults, the FLOOR_EXEMPT derivation, and the honesty register that records what does not hold — survives verification intact.
